# Bimanual and Torso-Assisted Manipulation

[Home](../../README.md) · [All categories](../README.md) · [简体中文](arm-torso-manipulation_cn.md)

Body Motion and Whole-Body Control Models → Bimanual and Torso-Assisted Manipulation

Manipulate objects through coordinated arm motions and support from the torso or other upper-body surfaces, including holding, regrasping and on-body object transfer. Record the learned policy outputs and the independent controllers used for the waist, legs, balance or locomotion; placement here does not imply unified whole-body actuation.

| [AM.WBC.ARM.TORSO.1] <a id="am-wbc-arm-torso-1"></a> | **WBD｜RL expert distillation · Diffusion policy · Command refinement**<br>[Whole-Body Dexterity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22184v1)<br>Conor Mc Gartoll, An Dang, Pranay Thangeda, Arjun Gupta, Carolina Higuera, Nima Fazeli, Mustafa Mukadam, Manikantan Nambi<br>**Tags:** `humanoid` `bimanual` `torso-assisted-manipulation` `regrasping` [reinforcement-learning](../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `expert-distillation` `diffusion-policy` `inverse-dynamics` `teleoperation` `command-refinement` `sim-to-real` | WBD formulates object repositioning supported by the arms and torso as transitions between holding states, uses RL experts to generate cross-body regrasping trajectories, and trains a diffusion motion prior with an inverse-dynamics model to refine coarse human commands into arm-joint actions that maintain object support.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Stable holding configurations are optimized and validated before per-object PPO experts learn transfers between left-, both- and right-arm holds; expert trajectories train a shared controller. It conditions on proprioceptive history and five geometry features, uses coarse commands for gradient guidance during diffusion, and maps generated arm-keypoint motions through inverse dynamics to 14 joint-target increments without per-step object pose. Expert training fixes the waist and legs, with fingers held closed. Hardware uses a human-teleoperated Unitree G1 with independent AMO lower-body and balance control. Simulation covers 15 geometric objects; hardware demonstrates shoulder touches and underarm stowing with a basketball and box, plus box transport. These results do not establish a jointly learned locomotion and whole-body manipulation policy. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22184v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-24 |
